claims.text: The proposed alloy is equiatomic Nb-Ta-Ti-Hf-Zr.
The starting alloy is a single-phase BCC solid solution.
The as-cast starting alloy has a nearly random elemental distribution.
Annealing Nb-Ta-Ti-Hf-Zr can produce nanoscale short-range chemical clustering or ordering.
Annealing at approximately 800 degrees Celsius for 12 hours followed by rapid quenching will produce detectable short-range order.
The specified annealing treatment will avoid secondary-phase formation.
The annealing-induced ordered regions will have a characteristic spacing of about 7-15 nm.
Atom probe tomography or advanced scattering can verify nanoscale chemical order.
Short-range chemical ordering reduces local lattice disorder.
Short-range chemical ordering reduces electron scattering in the alloy.
Reduced electron scattering improves Cooper-pair coherence.
Reduced pair-breaking scattering in locally ordered regions is the key factor enhancing superconductivity.
Annealing-induced short-range order will modestly increase the superconducting transition temperature relative to the as-cast alloy.
Annealing-induced short-range order will narrow the resistive superconducting transition relative to the as-cast alloy.
The as-cast Nb-Ta-Ti-Hf-Zr alloy has a superconducting transition temperature around 3-7 K.
The as-cast alloy has a relatively broad resistive transition because of high chemical disorder.
Excessive annealing may generate long-range ordered precipitates or secondary phases that obscure the proposed effect.

contradictions.description: The causal hypothesis would be directly challenged if annealing produced confirmed short-range order without improving Tc or transition width. The stated falsification rule instead requires both absent superconducting improvement and failure to confirm enhanced order; failure to induce the mediator means the proposed mediator-to-outcome mechanism was not actually tested.
